title: Batch importWorkspace's inserts: depth-batched nodes/issues, single createMany for fourteen flat tables

approvals.evidence: auto-approved: no protected path (lib/db/repo.ts is not in the protected-paths list -- lib/workspace.ts, lib/types.ts, lib/access.ts, middleware.ts, prisma/schema.prisma, migrations and .github/workflows are the only protected paths), no migration, no schema change

body.design_ref: None -- no open design question; Prisma's createMany is the framework's own documented batching primitive, already used elsewhere in this same function for scheduleAudit rows.

steps.title: Add byDepthBatches(items, state) next to depthOf: groups a HierarchyNode[]/Issue[] array into arrays bucketed by tree depth, sorted ascending by depth.
Replace the nodes and issues sort-then-per-row-create loops with byDepthBatches(...) + one createMany per depth bucket.
steps.verify_command: npx tsc --noEmit && npm run audit:persistence && npm run audit:rls

steps.title: Replace the fourteen flat per-row-create loops (activities, dependencies, relationships, evidence, notes, commitments, allocations, sows, notifications, approvals, timeEntries, estimates, estimateRevisions, engagements) with a filter (where the original loop had an inline continue) followed by one createMany call each, preserving the existing statement order between blocks (estimates before estimateRevisions, etc.).
steps.verify_command: npx tsc --noEmit && npm run audit:persistence && npm run audit:rls && npm run audit:integrity

steps.title: Full verification: tsc, tenancy, attribution, contracts, scenario suite, plus the three live-database proofs (persistence, rls, integrity) against the real configured database using self-cleaning proof tenants.
steps.verify_command: npx tsc --noEmit && npm run audit:tenancy && npm run audit:attribution && npm run audit:contracts && npm run validate:scenarios && npm run audit:persistence && npm run audit:rls && npm run audit:integrity

commit_boundaries: All four steps as one commit: one function, one coherent refactor (depth-batched tree tables plus fourteen flat tables), verified together against the live database rather than split into a partially-batched intermediate state.
body.rollback: Revert the single commit. Step 2 carries the only step where a mistake in depth-bucket grouping could violate the self-referencing foreign key (a child batched with or before its parent); verified against the live persistence and RLS proofs, which seed and read back a real multi-depth tree through the real database rather than a mock.
